page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores using the x86_64 architecture, powered by AMD EPYC 7542 processors running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and each physical core runs a single thread. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 6.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance tradeoffs. Single-core performance is a limitation, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the bottom 10% and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 25%. However, the massive core count compensates in parallel workloads, as evidenced by strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and a strong PassMark CPU score, both ranking in the top 25%. Memory performance is highly capable, with cached small-block read bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth scoring in the top 25%. Conversely, text processing and medium-model LLM text generation show weaker results, reflecting the lower single-core clock speed and shared CPU allocation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers high resource density for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated, non-shared CPU execution. The shared CPU model provides a massive pool of 64 cores and 384 GB of RAM at a lower qualitative cost tier than dedicated instances of similar scale. It is highly suited for highly parallelized tasks such as multi-threaded data decompression, Redis in-memory caching (where SET operations scored in the top 25%), software compilation, and general-purpose web serving. It is less suitable for single-threaded applications or real-time LLM text generation.
